tasks.locator: Results › Within-Treatment Drinking Outcomes for Pill-Taking Groups › Primary Outcomes, 2nd paragraph (p. 2009); Results › Within-Treatment Evaluation of CBI Therapy Without Pills (Placebo Effect), 2nd paragraph (p. 2011, continuing on p. 2012); Comment, 1st paragraph (p. 2013)
tasks.extracted: Given the naltrexone × CBI interaction, the authors state that the main-effect tests for naltrexone and CBI should be interpreted with caution (p. 2009). Corrected pairwise post hoc tests of percent days abstinent during treatment: placebo pills with medical management (73.8) against placebo pills with medical management plus CBI (79.8), P=.04; against CBI alone without pills or medical management (66.6), P=.03; placebo pills with medical management plus CBI against CBI alone, P<.001 (pp. 2011–2012). The authors' reading: patients receiving medical management did better when they also received either CBI or naltrexone; without CBI naltrexone helped, without naltrexone CBI helped, and the combination did not further improve outcomes (p. 2013).
